text:
sara: Customer ran a scale test and started seeing 429 spikes, mostly against the 64k-capable model. Reported pattern: ~1.4k RPM sustained with short spikes to ~3k RPM over ~3 min, overall concurrency peaking ~200. Any immediate pointers?

jamal: Do we have a request sample and the exact model names/variants used? Sounds like model-specific RPM/TPM + concurrency hitting limits when fanouting.

sara: Here’s the curl they used (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \\n  -d '{"model":"open-64k-xl","input":"<~32k chars of context + prefetch docs>","stream":false}'
```
They also prefetch 2 extra docs per request (fanout) and do parallel calls to three model variants: open-8k, open-32k, open-64k. Streaming disabled.

priya: Two quick notes: 1) Per-model RPM/TPM quotas are enforced independently; heavy fanout can push one model over its window even if overall RPM looks fine. 2) Long-context variants (64k) typically have lower effective max concurrency due to memory/KV cache pressure, so you'll see queueing -> 429s sooner.

jamal: Confirming from logs: we see repeated 429 responses with body: `\{"error\":\"RateLimit\", \"model\":\"open-64k-xl\", \"reason\":\"per_model_tpm_exceeded\"}` and trace ids like `trace-0a1b2c3d`. Also a handful of 401s interleaved that look like transient auth refresh failures from the customer's infra during high load.

mike-support: I started a repro run on our test cluster following their profile and reproduced 429s ~30s into the spike, concentrated on the 64k variant. Collected traces and stack traces, linked to SUP-4321.

jamal: Repro checklist I recommend customers try (minimal script):
1) Single client, fanout to three models at target RPM (e.g., 1400 RPM total split evenly)
2) Introduce short spike (2–3 minutes) to 3k RPM
3) Keep request concurrency capped at X per model (start low and ramp)
4) Collect response codes, trace ids, and per-request model name
We use this to map which model's per-model window is tripping.

priya: Mitigations for support to recommend to customers: 
- Reduce fanout or serialize prefetch across models.
- Add exponential backoff + jitter on 429s.
- Pin to a lower-context variant (e.g., open-32k) for high-throughput endpoints.
- Enable prefix/KV caching where possible to cut token compute.
- Consider Dedicated capacity or an isolated pool if you need sustained high TPS on a long-context model.

jamal: Also note: there's a short burst allowance (a small burst window) but sustained spikes will exhaust the sliding-window TPM. For diagnostics, ask for per-minute request counts per model and per-client API key. That tells us whether it's a per-model TPM or global throttle.

mike-support: I added a small bash repro and uploaded artifacts to the ticket. Sample snippet we ran: 
```
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do \
  curl ... &
  sleep 0.06
done
wait
```
This produced 429s after ~25s against open-64k-xl.

priya: On the support playbook side, escalate to eng-runtime only if we see: repeated 429s after client applies recommended backoff, or if trace ids show internal queue timeouts rather than immediate throttles. Otherwise the right fix is traffic shaping / dedicated pool.

sara: Customer agreed to run the repro with our script and add backoff+pinning. I've opened SUP-4321 and attached logs. Will update thread after their run tomorrow. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy: infra/ratelimit-service v2.13 rolled out to prod (no changes to model windowing).

jamal: Thanks — once customer results arrive we can check for remaining 401s (auth) vs model-rate 429s. If 401s persist, ask them to rotate keys and test under low load to rule out token refresh bugs.

sara: Sounds good. Closing here for now, will reopen if repro shows unexpected behavior.
